summary_en: This note introduces a core guiding idea in analysis: understanding difficult objects through approximation, framed as "give yourself an epsilon of room." It explains how epsilon-based reasoning underlies basic facts about real numbers and motivates the definition and use of limits, especially for sequences.

problems.statement_en:
Example 0.1: Prove that
$$x=0 \iff |x|<\varepsilon,\ \forall \varepsilon>0.$$ In particular, explain why $$\forall \varepsilon>0,\ |x|<\varepsilon \implies x=0.$$
problems.statement_zh: 例子0.1：$$x=0\iff |x|<\varepsilon,\forall \varepsilon>0$$我们主要看右边的部分，为何$|x|<\varepsilon,\forall \varepsilon\implies x=0$。

problems.statement_en:
Proposition 0.2: Establish the following epsilon characterizations:
1. $$\forall \varepsilon>0,\ x<a+\varepsilon \implies x\le a.$$
2. $$b>0\ \text{and}\ (\forall \varepsilon>0,\ x<a+b\varepsilon) \implies x\le a.$$
3. $$\forall \varepsilon>0,\ x>a-\varepsilon \implies x\ge a.$$
4. $$b>0\ \text{and}\ (\forall \varepsilon>0,\ x>a-b\varepsilon) \implies x\ge a.$$
5. $$\forall \varepsilon>0,\ |x-a|<\varepsilon \implies x=a.$$
6. $$b>0\ \text{and}\ (\forall \varepsilon>0,\ |x-a|<b\varepsilon) \implies x=a.$$
problems.statement_zh: 命题0.2：1. $$\forall \varepsilon>0,x<a+\varepsilon\implies x\leq a$$ 2. $$b>0\text{ and }(\forall \varepsilon>0,x<a+b\varepsilon)\implies x\leq a$$ 3. $$\forall \varepsilon>0,x>a-\varepsilon\implies x\geq a$$ 4. $$b>0\text{ and }(\forall \varepsilon>0,x>a-b\varepsilon)\implies x\geq a$$ 5. $$\forall \varepsilon>0,|x-a|<\varepsilon\implies x= a$$ 6. $$b>0\text{ and }(\forall \varepsilon>0,|x-a|<b\varepsilon)\implies x= a$$
key_techniques: epsilon characterization of order and equality

problems.statement_en:
Example 1.1.1: Define
$$a_n:=\sum_{k=0}^{n}\frac{1}{k!}.$$Study whether this sequence grows beyond every positive real number or instead stays below and converges to a positive real number; assuming the limit is $e$, explain how the limit definition allows one to approximate $e$ within any prescribed absolute error $\varepsilon$ by choosing a suitable partial sum $a_n$.
problems.statement_zh: 例子1.1.1：定义序列$$a_n:=\sum_{k=0}^{n}\frac{1}{k!}$$讨论这个序列是会永无止境地增长到比任何一个具体的正实数更大，还是说会永远小于但无限接近于某个正实数；假设这个正实数为$e$，说明如何利用极限定义通过合适的$a_n$对$e$作绝对误差小于给定$\varepsilon$的估计。
key_techniques: approximating an infinite object by finite partial sums
